text:
Maria: Heads-up — a couple of customers pushed back: they need structured-output + function-calling parity across Python/TS SDKs. We should nail scope + launch gating before the next release.
Ashley: Which customers & concrete blockers?
Maria: Acme and FinCo. Blockers: nested structured types (arrays of objects), streaming tool calls with schema validation, and clear examples showing fallback when schema mismatch occurs.
Chris: For TS I'd do discriminated unions; for Python TypedDicts + pydantic models as examples. Minimal API change: add `structured_schema` param + `validate_output=True` flag.
Liam: Agree. Keep default `validate_output=False` for GA to avoid breaking apps. Document the opt-in path.
Maria: Proposed rollout playbook: 1) concise TS types + examples 2) Python stubs and mypy examples 3) sample prompt set + eval harness 4) docs + changelog + migration guide.
Ashley: :thumbsup: tentative timeline?
Maria: Draft PRs in 2 weeks, 1 week internal review, 48h canary across dev orgs, GA once eval regressions <=5% and no customer blocking bugs.
Chris: Canary config suggestion: route 5% traffic via feature-flag `structured_output_v2`. SDKs should auto-fallback to raw text if validation fails.
Liam: Quick TS example for types + tests:
```
// types.ts
export type ImageTag = { label: string; confidence: number }
export type ModelResponse = { images: ImageTag[] }
```
Add unit tests that replay failing prompts.
Maria: I'll own the eval harness and prompt set. Who takes changelog + examples?
Ashley: I can draft the changelog + release notes + migration guide. Will include an explicit snippet showing old->new behavior.
Chris: I'll own TS types + examples. Note: codegen pipeline currently strips nested optional fields — opening an infra ticket.
Maria: If infra blocks us, fallback: ship docs that export manual types and a short migration script. Keep PRs small.
devex-bot: Reminder — sprint deadline in 2 weeks. Please attach PRs to milestone `structured-output-ga`.
Ashley: One more ask from support: provide a small runnable example for customers that shows function-calling -> structured output -> typed deserialization.
Maria: Yes, migration guide + runnable example will be included. I'll draft migration section and a gist.
Liam: I'll start Python stubs and tests today.
Chris: :raised_hands: plan to open TS PR by EOD next Tues.
Maria: Target merge window for canary (symbolic): 1743659000 — actual schedule will follow CI signals.
Ashley: Sounds good. I'll block time next Friday for docs review.
Maria: Thanks — assigning owners: Chris (TS types/examples), Liam (Py stubs/tests), Ashley (changelog/docs/migration), Maria (evals + rollout). We'll sync in next standup.
